title: Activity and Fragment leaks
key_conclusions: Activity leaks should be diagnosed as destroyed Activity objects that remain strongly reachable from a GC Root after onDestroy.
Fragment View leaks are usually view-lifecycle boundary failures: the Fragment may still be valid while the old View tree should have been released at onDestroyView.
The practical fix point is the owner or bridge edge, such as a singleton field, delayed message, observer, adapter callback, binding field, or animation listener.
A fix should be accepted only with before/after evidence from retained paths, LeakCanary traces, heap dump instance counts, or dumpsys meminfo trends.
shallow_points: The article still uses representative retained-path examples rather than a real target-app HPROF.
It does not decode a real LeakCanary Activity or Fragment trace line by line.
It does not validate AndroidX Fragment internal field names against a specific dependency version.
Compose-specific lifecycle and remember/effect leak patterns are only named as a boundary, not analyzed.
